h1_question: Is selective proposal acceptance / abstention, with all other scientific axes frozen, sufficient to make the current GT-free regional path a credible standalone revision?
h1_question_clarification: H1 does NOT ask whether selectivity helps at all; it asks whether selectivity ALONE adequately resolves the Phase 13 deployable failure while retaining meaningful regional utility.

A.name: GLOBAL_PRESERVATION
A.question: Does selective abstention remove the catastrophic FP / precision cost and restore acceptable global preservation?
A.finding: NO. Every one of the 28 config/model combinations has policy macro Dice BELOW GLOBAL (28/28). The most aggressive policy (R1-C5) still trails GLOBAL by -0.131136 (UNet), -0.143855 (Attention U-Net), -0.157948 (UNet++) and -0.133755 (DeepLabV3+). Selectivity sharply reduces the FP burden (mean FP delta falls from +7778 to about +2049, a 74% reduction) and roughly halves the Dice deficit, but the burden remains POSITIVE for every policy and the deficit is never closed. Case worsening is essentially unchanged: 93.0-94.5 of 103 cases worsen under every policy.

B.name: REGIONAL_UTILITY_RETENTION
B.question: Does any selective policy retain genuine component / empty recovery benefit beyond GLOBAL?
B.finding: PARTIALLY, AND NOT SUFFICIENTLY. Component losses are 0 for every policy and every architecture, and empty recoveries are largely retained (C0 8/3/5/11 vs C5 8/3/5/10). But component recoveries collapse under aggressive selectivity: 16/9/14/16 at C0 (55 total) down to 2/1/3/4 at C1 and C5 (10 total) - an 82% loss of the recovery signal. RETENTION_DICE is negative for ALL 28 config/model combinations, so no policy converts the oracle mechanism into positive deployable benefit.
B.retention_note: never clipped; negative values preserved as measured

C.name: INTERVENTION_SELECTIVITY
C.question: Does the policy reduce off-target proposal intervention?
C.finding: YES - this is the dimension H1 clearly improves. Accepted proposals fall 494 -> 102 (C0 -> C5), GT-miss accepted proposals fall 372 -> 68, mean accepted proposals per image fall 4.796 -> 0.990, and mean intervention union area falls 0.004846 -> 0.001486. Mean policy precision rises from 0.2342 to 0.4259 while mean recall is essentially unchanged (0.6664 -> 0.6502). Selectivity therefore does improve intervention precision. However the accepted GT-miss FRACTION remains 0.666667 (68/102) versus 0.753036 (372/494) at C0 - a real improvement, but two thirds of the surviving interventions are still off-target.
C.membership_label_blind: YES - GT fields are post-freeze descriptive evaluation only

D.name: CROSS_ARCHITECTURE_CONSISTENCY
D.question: Does the behaviour generalize across all four architectures?
D.finding: GENERAL, NOT ARCHITECTURE-SPECIFIC. The negative Dice-vs-GLOBAL behaviour holds in all four architectures for every policy (28/28 below GLOBAL). At R1-C5, cases worse in all four = 84 of 103, components recovered by >=1 architecture = 6, recovered by all four = 1, and components lost by >=1 architecture = 0. The mitigation is also consistent: every architecture improves under aggressive selectivity and loses recovery at the same time. No architecture is a winner, no ranking is made.

trade_off_adjudication.pattern_tested: MILD selectivity preserves recovery but barely relieves the global Dice / FP failure; AGGRESSIVE selectivity substantially relieves FP but removes most component-recovery benefit and still remains below GLOBAL.
trade_off_adjudication.mild_evidence: C2 reproduces the C0 recovery profile exactly (16/9/14/16) while relieving only 2% of the FP burden (+7778 -> +7598); C4 keeps 52 of 55 recoveries and relieves 8%; C6 keeps 41 of 55 and relieves 12%. Mean macro Dice moves only 0.2999 -> 0.3054 / 0.3219 / 0.3314.
trade_off_adjudication.aggressive_evidence: C1 and C5 relieve 73-74% of the FP burden (+7778 -> +2075 / +2049) and lift mean macro Dice to 0.4608 / 0.4645, but total component recoveries fall 55 -> 10 (an 82% loss) and all four architectures remain below GLOBAL.

reasoning: Dimension C is clearly positive: selective acceptance does improve intervention precision (accepted 494 -> 102; GT-miss accepted 372 -> 68; mean precision 0.2342 -> 0.4259; FP burden reduced 74%). Dimensions A and B are materially improved but NOT resolved: every one of the 28 config/model combinations still has policy macro Dice below GLOBAL, the most aggressive policy still trails GLOBAL by 0.131-0.158, the FP burden remains positive for every policy, and RETENTION_DICE is negative in all 28 combinations. The trade-off is strict: mild selectivity preserves the recovery profile (C2 identical to C0) but relieves almost none of the FP burden, while aggressive selectivity relieves 74% of the FP burden but destroys 82% of the component recoveries. No frozen policy jointly restores global preservation AND retains enough regional utility. Selective acceptance alone is therefore a real but PARTIAL mitigation, insufficient as a standalone revision. This does NOT establish a representation failure: H1 isolated the acceptance-only axis, and its insufficiency leaves localizer representation, heatmap confidence calibration, proposal ranking, training objective, checkpoint-selection semantics and precision/recall balance as open contributors for H2 protocol design.

h2_eligibility.reason: H1 has isolated the acceptance-only axis and shown it is not sufficient by itself; this does NOT prove representation failure.
